PullRequest.Title: ci: remove the required-checks job now that PR Gate is the required check
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Follow-up to #344110. Branch protection on `main` and `release/**/*` now requires **PR Gate** instead of the per-OS `<OS> / <job>` checks, so the `required-checks` job in `pr.yml` only duplicates PR Gate. This PR removes it.

## Changes
- **`pr.yml`**: delete the `required-checks` job. Update the comments that described it or the workarounds for the old required checks ("Until branch protection requires only PR Gate…", "reports as part of `Windows / Electron`", "per-OS required checks").
- **`pr-linux-cli-test.yml`**: drop the comments saying the `CLI` name and inner `if:` exist so the required `Linux / CLI` check reports. The behavior is unchanged.
- **`detectChanges.test.ts`**: the tests read the job-to-output mapping from the `required-checks` matrix. They now assert each core test job's `needs`/`if` directly, as one snapshot of job → change-detection output, and that every output is declared. The PR Gate test no longer excludes `required-checks`.
- **Skills / test comment**: update `smoke-tests` and `fix-ci-failures` skills and an `agentHostTestSelection.test.ts` comment that referred to the old checks.

## Notes for reviewers
- PR Gate already `needs` every job, so nothing it covers changes. The per-job checks such as `Linux (run) / Electron` keep reporting as before. Only the duplicate `Linux / Electron`-style checks go away.
- Existing release branches keep their own copy of `pr.yml`, so this does not affect them.

## Testing
- `cd build && node --test lib/test/detectChanges.test.ts lib/test/agentHostTestSelection.test.ts`: 20/20 passed.
- I broke `pr.yml` on purpose to check that the rewritten tests still catch errors. Each case below made the expected test fail:
  - a job wired to the wrong change-detection output
  - an `if:` replaced with `always()`
  - a macOS/Windows unit job skipping on `unit-tests` instead of `selected-unit-tests`
  - a job dropped from PR Gate's `needs`
- `cd build && npm run typecheck`: passed.
- `npm run eslint -- build/lib/test/detectChanges.test.ts build/lib/test/agentHostTestSelection.test.ts`: passed.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: One PR workflow fanned out result aggregation into a 15-entry matrix of hosted runner jobs, duplicating runner startup and status-processing work already performed by PR Gate.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Every pull request incurred 15 redundant GitHub Actions runner startups and associated compute/status-processing overhead after its core tests.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: Deleting the entire `required-checks` matrix removes 15 duplicate hosted-runner allocations and their shell/jq work from every PR workflow while retaining one aggregate PR Gate job.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: The deleted `required-checks` job used a 15-entry matrix, so every PR workflow allocated up to 15 additional ubuntu-24.04 runners after the core test jobs completed. Each matrix child started a shell and repeatedly invoked jq only to re-report job results under legacy names. The unchanged `pr-gate` job already depends on every workflow job and performs the same result aggregation once, and branch protection now requires that single gate.

Scenarios.Scenario: Pull-request CI result aggregation and merge gating
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Core test jobs complete first; the unchanged PR Gate then waits on every workflow job and aggregates their results before the required check can pass. The deleted required-checks matrix also waited on core tests but, after branch protection moved to PR Gate, its legacy checks were off the merge critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: .github/workflows/pr.yml deleted required-checks job at base line 562
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Allocate GitHub-hosted Ubuntu runners for result-reporting jobs
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Before: 15 matrix runner allocations per PR workflow, plus the existing PR Gate runner. After: zero legacy reporting runners and one PR Gate runner.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The required-checks 15-entry matrix allocated a separate hosted runner for each legacy OS/check combination.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The deleted runners no longer delay legacy status publication or consume CI capacity; with PR Gate now the required check, they were not needed for merge progress.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: .github/workflows/pr.yml deleted required-checks Check job results step
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run bash and repeated jq processes to decode needs and matrix parts
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Before: one shell per each of 15 matrix children, with jq calls per represented job; after: this entire set is removed. The unchanged PR Gate runs one shell and one jq stream.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Fifteen matrix children each performed their own JSON parsing and status loop in addition to PR Gate's aggregation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Removed duplicate post-test processing; the remaining single PR Gate subprocess is on the required-check critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One invocation per PR workflow run. Before the diff, one logical legacy result-reporting step expanded to 15 matrix children; after the diff, only the single existing PR Gate aggregation remains.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Previously, up to 15 independent ubuntu-24.04 matrix children became schedulable as their dependencies completed, in addition to the single PR Gate runner. The diff removes that burst; PR Gate remains one runner with a serial loop over its needs.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Neither aggregation path has a reusable cache or coalescing state. Each workflow run starts fresh; warm and cold behavior are therefore equivalent. The diff coalesces reporting structurally into the already-existing PR Gate rather than adding a cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the deleted matrix, runner type, dependencies, shell, jq loop, and unchanged single PR Gate are all directly visible in the workflow.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact hosted-runner queue/startup time and billed duration vary by GitHub Actions load, but the removed cardinality of 15 runner jobs per PR run is explicit in the matrix.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression. This is a concrete boundary-fanout improvement, recorded separately as a regression fix.

Scenarios.Scenario: Local/CI execution of detectChanges workflow-structure tests
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each affected test synchronously reads and parses pr.yml, then performs assertions. The changed core-job assertion filters the already-parsed jobs object and applies a small regex; this remains on the test's critical path but is bounded by the workflow's few dozen jobs.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read for each existing loadWorkflow call; the changed tests still call it once apiece, so the diff does not increase boundary cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same tests synchronously loaded the same workflow file before inspecting required-checks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The read is on each test's critical path, but its frequency and placement are unchanged.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of jobs in pr.yml (currently a few dozen) and 19 reusable core test jobs after effective filtering. The prior assertion iterated the 15 required-check matrix entries and their parts; the new assertion performs a few linear passes over the jobs object.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No new concurrency or burst is introduced. These calculations are synchronous within the node:test case; surrounding test-runner scheduling is unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: loadWorkflow does not cache and synchronously rereads/parses pr.yml on each calling test both before and after the diff. The new helper has no retained cache or negative-cache behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: call counts and collection bounds are directly visible; no new subprocess, network, IPC, database, or additional filesystem operation is introduced by the changed assertions.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact YAML parse and assertion duration is unmeasured, but both collection sizes are small and repository-bounded; the changed extra linear scans cannot realistically dominate the pre-existing file read/YAML parse or test suite.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new O(number of workflow jobs) in-memory scans replace O(required-check entries/parts) scans at small bounded cardinality without adding an expensive boundary.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: When affected, checkout, Rust installation/update, clippy, and tests remain on the CLI job's critical path; when unaffected, the existing job-level if still skips all work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Checkout repository and download/update the Rust toolchain
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Unchanged: at most one checkout and Rust installation/update sequence per affected caller; zero when inputs.affected is false.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical job-level if, checkout, curl/rustup, lint, and test behavior; only explanatory comments were removed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These operations remain on the affected CLI test critical path and are still skipped for unaffected changes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One reusable CLI workflow job per configured caller; no changed executable input or multiplicity.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Unchanged single linux-cli-test job per caller; the diff only deletes comments and does not alter scheduling.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache behavior changes. Existing checkout and Rust toolchain network behavior remains exactly as before.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the diff removes comments only in this workflow.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material for causality: runtime YAML is unchanged.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all six changed files and all diff pages. The executable workflow change removes a 15-way duplicate hosted-runner fan-out already covered by PR Gate; test changes add only bounded in-memory scans with unchanged filesystem reads, and the remaining edits are documentation/comments. No performance finding was submitted; one concrete CI performance regression fix was recorded.
